lessons.title: m, a, t
lessons.detail: The first three letters are introduced together so reading can begin immediately.

lessons.title: Ending in S
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases
lessons.detail: Final s can spell /s/ or /z/ and can mark more than one.

lessons.title: e
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases

lessons.title: h
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases

lessons.title: Heart Words
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases
lessons.detail: Introduces high-frequency words with spellings not yet taught.

lessons.title: l
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases

lessons.title: c
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases

lessons.title: u
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases
lessons.detail: Completes the five short-vowel letters.

lessons.title: r
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases
lessons.detail: for and are appear constantly in real books, so they are learned early by heart; their spellings are explained with Bossy R in Module 8.

lessons.title: z
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases

lessons.title: Module 2 Review
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases

lessons.title: sh
lessons.detail: sh spells one sound.

lessons.title: ch, tch
lessons.detail: One sound, two spellings. tch commonly follows a short vowel.

lessons.title: y
lessons.detail: Introduces y as a consonant.

lessons.title: k, ck
lessons.detail: One /k/ sound, two spellings. ck commonly follows a short vowel and never means two /k/s.

lessons.title: qu
lessons.detail: q is paired with u.

lessons.title: f
lessons.detail: f spells /f/.

lessons.title: ff, ll, ss, zz
lessons.detail: Doubled letters make one sound.

lessons.title: th — both sounds
lessons.detail: th has voiced and unvoiced sounds.

lessons.title: w, wh
lessons.detail: Introduces w and wh.

lessons.title: ng and nk
lessons.detail: ng and nk are read as glued chunks. Only true short-vowel chunks appear here: a and i shift before ng and nk, so -ing comes next lesson and ink/ank come early in Module 5.

lessons.title: -ing
lessons.detail: The glued -ing chunk: first in one-beat words, then as an ending that adds a beat. Only clean base + ing words here — no doubling (running) or drop-e (making) bases; those wait for Lesson 54.

lessons.title: Meet the Vowels
lessons.detail: Vowels can spell short sounds or their names.

lessons.title: Magic E → i_e
lessons.detail: The final e is silent and makes the preceding vowel long.

lessons.title: j + dge
lessons.detail: j and dge spell /j/; dge commonly follows a short vowel.

lessons.title: a_e
lessons.detail: a_e spells /ā/.

lessons.title: v
lessons.detail: v spells /v/.

lessons.title: o_e
lessons.detail: o_e spells /ō/.

lessons.title: x
lessons.detail: Completes all 26 letters.

lessons.title: u_e
lessons.detail: u_e spells long u.

lessons.title: e_e
lessons.detail: e_e is a rare spelling of /ē/.

lessons.title: -old and -ost
lessons.detail: In these small word families, o spells /ō/ before two consonants. Treat them as families, not a general rule.

lessons.title: -ind and -ild
lessons.detail: In these small word families, i spells /ī/ before two consonants. Treat them as families, not a general rule.

lessons.title: Lowercase letters
lessons.detail: Consolidates lowercase forms, especially letters whose shapes differ from their capitals.

lessons.title: ink and ing
lessons.detail: i shifts its sound before nk and ng, so ink and ing are read as glued chunks. ing returns from Lesson 31, now in lowercase.

lessons.title: ank and ang
lessons.detail: a shifts its sound before nk and ng, so ank and ang are read as glued chunks.

lessons.title: Soft c
lessons.detail: c followed by e commonly spells /s/.

lessons.title: Soft g
lessons.detail: g followed by e commonly spells /j/.

lessons.title: Reading Two-Syllable Words
lessons.detail: Extends two-syllable reading beyond -ing words, in three rungs: two known words, then a known chunk + a known word (un- means not; re- means again), then true splits.

lessons.title: -es endings
lessons.detail: After s, x, sh, ch, or tch, plural -es spells /iz/ and adds a syllable.

lessons.title: Consonant-le
lessons.detail: Final consonant-le forms a common unstressed syllable.

lessons.title: -ed endings
lessons.detail: -ed marks past tense and can spell /t/, /d/, or /id/.

lessons.title: Endings that change the base
lessons.detail: Before -ing or -ed, a base can double its last consonant or drop its Magic E. A doubled consonant keeps the vowel short; a single consonant hints the vowel is long. Completes the -ing story from Lesson 31.

lessons.title: Open chunks
lessons.detail: Open syllables use long vowels; unstressed vowels may reduce to /uh/.

lessons.title: Vowel Y
lessons.detail: Final y commonly spells /ī/ in short words and /ē/ in longer words.

lessons.title: Module 5 Review
lessons.detail: Review plus the first timed fluency check.

lessons.title: Vowel Teams → ee
lessons.detail: Two vowels can work together to spell one sound.

lessons.title: ea
lessons.detail: ea commonly spells /ē/ and sometimes /ĕ/.

lessons.title: ai
lessons.detail: The /ā/ vowel team used inside words. Revisit said, learned by heart in Module 3.

lessons.title: ay
lessons.detail: ay commonly spells /ā/ at word ends.

lessons.title: oa
lessons.detail: oa spells /ō/.

lessons.title: oo — both sounds
lessons.detail: oo has two common sounds.

lessons.title: aw
lessons.detail: The /aw/ sound at the ends and inside words.

lessons.title: au
lessons.detail: A second spelling of /aw/, usually inside words.

lessons.title: all and al
lessons.detail: all is a dependable chunk. al can spell the sound in always or the sound in calm; in walk and talk, l is silent.

lessons.title: Just-Read Day I
lessons.detail: Fluency practice; no new spelling.

lessons.title: ie — both sounds
lessons.detail: ie commonly spells /ī/ at word ends and /ē/ inside words.

lessons.title: igh
lessons.detail: igh spells /ī/.

lessons.title: ou — four sounds
lessons.detail: ou can spell the vowel sounds in out, soup, young, or could.

lessons.title: ow — both sounds
lessons.detail: ow spells the sound in cow or the /ō/ sound in snow.

lessons.title: oi
lessons.detail: The /oy/ sound inside words.

lessons.title: oy
lessons.detail: The same sound at word-ends.

lessons.title: ew
lessons.detail: ew commonly spells long u or /oo/.

lessons.title: ue
lessons.detail: ue commonly spells long u or /oo/ at word ends.

lessons.title: Contractions
lessons.detail: An apostrophe marks omitted letters.

lessons.title: Just-Read Day II
lessons.detail: Fluency practice; no new spelling.

lessons.title: Bossy R → ar
lessons.detail: r changes the sound of the vowel before it; ar spells /ar/. Revisit are, learned by heart in Module 2.

lessons.title: or
lessons.detail: or spells /or/. Revisit for, learned by heart in Module 2 and now fully decodable.

lessons.title: er
lessons.detail: er commonly spells /er/, especially in final syllables.

lessons.title: ir
lessons.detail: A second spelling of the /er/ sound.

lessons.title: ur
lessons.detail: er, ir, and ur spell the same /er/ sound.

lessons.title: ar and or can say /er/
lessons.detail: In an unstressed final syllable, ar or or can spell /er/.

lessons.title: are
lessons.detail: are spells the r-controlled sound in care.

lessons.title: air
lessons.detail: air spells the same r-controlled sound as are.

lessons.title: ear — four sounds
lessons.detail: ear can spell the r-controlled sounds in bear, hear, heard, or heart.

lessons.title: ore
lessons.detail: A second spelling of the /or/ sound.

lessons.title: -er & -est
lessons.detail: -er compares two; -est compares three or more.

lessons.title: Just-Read Day III
lessons.detail: Fluency practice; no new spelling.

lessons.title: eigh
lessons.detail: A rare but real spelling of /ā/.

lessons.title: ph
lessons.detail: A rare second spelling of /f/, mostly in Greek-origin words.

lessons.title: aught
lessons.detail: A dependable /awt/ chunk in a small word family.

lessons.title: ough
lessons.detail: A focused set of high-frequency words in which ough has several pronunciations.

lessons.title: oe
lessons.detail: oe can spell /ō/; in heroes, poem, and poet, o and e cross an ending or syllable boundary.

lessons.title: ey — both sounds
lessons.detail: ey can spell /ē/ as in key or /ā/ as in they. Their is introduced here as a related heart word after they is secure, not as an ey example.

lessons.title: Just-Read Day IV
lessons.detail: Fluency and expression practice; no new spelling.

lessons.title: kn
lessons.detail: The k is silent.

lessons.title: wr
lessons.detail: The w is silent.

lessons.title: mb
lessons.detail: The final b is silent.

lessons.title: Three-syllable words
lessons.detail: Extends syllable reading to three-syllable words.

lessons.title: Choose your own book
lessons.detail: Independent-book selection and reading practice.

lessons.title: Cumulative Review
lessons.detail: Cumulative review and Fluency Check IV.

lessons.title: Graduation 🎓
lessons.detail: Independent final reading and graduation.
